trigger: Previous span-variance audit hit eta4 upper bound in all five train folds and full fit; its validation/private residuals are already exposed development results.
hypothesis: Long-span heteroscedastic covariance may improve count residual likelihood, but eta4 may be only a boundary artifact or proxy for shared demand-level error.
extended_search: 17-point eta grid[-4,12], bounded local refinement around best point; keep better grid/refinement. Fixed4/8/12 controls retained.
demand_control: Normalized convex covariance mixture of additive independent path covariance and rank-one (Ab)(Ab).T, weight0..0.9999 fit on training roads; random global demand-scale error control, not direct OD truth.
mean: Zero fixed for every model; one shared variance profiled only on training roads.
validation: Five public-train leave-family folds; full models frozen before evaluating supplied validation/private public inputs. This is follow-up development, not fresh blind data. All six models reported, no path candidate or official gain claim.
scope: Observable count uncertainty alone does not identify OD pairing or nullspace errors. Official Task4 baseline unchanged, Kaggle uploads prohibited.
